short_definition: A lightweight governed engineering framework for Microsoft Fabric.
long_definition: FabricOps packages reusable notebooks, governed read/write orchestration, Data Contracts, Data Agreements, and shared metadata so teams can run governed Fabric pipelines without rebuilding the same engineering and governance plumbing.
preferred_usage: Use as the public project name.
avoid_usage: full data product platform

short_definition: A versioned agreement between provider and recipient Data Stewards that defines why data may be shared and used.
long_definition: In FabricOps, a Data Agreement records the provider and recipient Data Stewards, purpose, approved uses, validity, and supporting governance context. An activated Data Contract links to the exact Data Agreement version that authorizes Production use.
preferred_usage: Use data agreement for the steward-to-steward governance relationship that starts the FabricOps workflow.
avoid_usage: data contract when table-level guarantees are meant

short_definition: A versioned set of governed expectations for one table.
long_definition: A FabricOps Data Contract is authored for one table_id. A frozen version captures its schema, processing settings, enrichment, and guardrails. After validation, that exact version can be activated for Production and linked to a Data Agreement version.
preferred_usage: Use data contract for table-level governed expectations; describe Data Agreement linkage only at activation.
avoid_usage: data agreement when the steward-to-steward sharing relationship is meant

short_definition: Descriptive business and governance metadata added to a governed table or column.
long_definition: FabricOps Enrichment stores descriptions and information classifications for a Data Contract version. It adds context but does not enforce pipeline behaviour; runtime requirements belong in Guardrails.
preferred_usage: Use enrichment for business and governance information added to the Data Catalogue.
avoid_usage: metadata enrichment when enrichment is sufficient

short_definition: Versioned rules that FabricOps checks during governed pipeline execution.
long_definition: FabricOps Guardrails define runtime expectations such as Schema, Freshness, Source Drift, Data Quality, and Sensitive Data treatment. Each rule can be configured to warn or block when its expectation is not met.
preferred_usage: Use guardrails for the governed rules FabricOps evaluates; use singular only for grammar.
avoid_usage: generic policy when a FabricOps Guardrail is meant

short_definition: A Guardrail that applies an explicit treatment to a governed column before write.
long_definition: FabricOps Sensitive Data rules apply one configured treatment to a column before a governed write: tokenize, mask, bucket, or remove. Information Classification remains descriptive and does not trigger treatment by itself.
preferred_usage: Use Sensitive Data Guardrail for explicit Tokenize, Mask, Bucket, or Remove column treatment; use Classification for descriptive sensitivity labels.
avoid_usage: anonymize or redact when the implemented treatment can be named precisely

short_definition: Evaluating active Guardrails during a pipeline run and applying their configured action.
long_definition: FabricOps enforcement runs the relevant Guardrails at read or write boundaries. A failed rule can warn or block according to its configuration.
preferred_usage: Use enforcement for applying active Guardrails during execution.
avoid_usage: validation when the runtime action on a Guardrail result is meant

short_definition: The outcome of a Guardrail evaluation during a pipeline run.
long_definition: FabricOps returns the evaluated rule outcome and resulting status or pipeline decision so the caller can inspect what passed, warned, or blocked.
preferred_usage: Use guardrail result for the recorded outcome of a FabricOps Guardrail evaluation.
avoid_usage: rule result

short_definition: Representing governance decisions as structured metadata that engineering can directly use.
long_definition: FabricOps stores Data Agreements, Data Contracts, Enrichment, and Guardrails as structured metadata. Governed pipelines resolve that same metadata during validation and execution instead of relying only on separate prose documentation.
preferred_usage: Use governance as code when governance decisions are represented as structured FabricOps metadata that engineering can directly consume and enforce.
avoid_usage: using governance as code for ordinary documentation that has no executable or metadata-driven connection to the workflow

short_definition: Keeping reusable pipeline logic separate from environment-specific Fabric configuration.
long_definition: 00_env_config maps logical stores to the Fabric items for the active environment. The same 02_pipeline can therefore move between environments without hard-coded workspace IDs, item IDs, paths, or endpoints throughout the notebook.
preferred_usage: Use configuration-driven engineering for the separation of reusable pipeline logic from environment-specific targets, paths, IDs, and repeatable processing settings.
avoid_usage: using configuration-driven engineering to mean that all business transformation logic must be configurable

short_definition: The three user-facing stages of the standard 02_pipeline: Read, Transform, and Write.
long_definition: Read uses FabricOps governed read orchestration, Transform contains project-owned PySpark logic, and Write uses governed write orchestration. Source and target describe dataset roles, not additional notebook stages.
preferred_usage: Use Read, Transform, and Write for 02_pipeline stage names; use source and target only for the technical dataset, lineage, processing, or configuration concepts they describe.
avoid_usage: Extract or Load as user-facing 02_pipeline stage labels

short_definition: A read that loads the complete selected source dataset for the run.
long_definition: FabricOps returns the complete selected source without a project-owned source filter or incremental scope.
preferred_usage: Use full dataset when distinguishing a complete input from an explicitly filtered project-owned query.
avoid_usage: incremental read configuration

short_definition: The governed method used to write a target table.
long_definition: FabricOps supports four load strategies: overwrite, append, SCD1, and SCD2. The target Data Contract stores the selected strategy and any required parameters.
preferred_usage: Use load strategy for governed target write behaviour.
avoid_usage: source pattern or Source Drift behaviour as a second strategy

short_definition: The Microsoft Fabric schedule configured to run a notebook.
long_definition: FabricOps reads notebook schedule metadata from Fabric. It is operational metadata, not a Data Contract setting, and is separate from the Freshness expectation for source data.
preferred_usage: Use scheduled refresh for discovered Fabric execution timing, and Freshness for the independently authored source-data arrival expectation.
avoid_usage: an editable Data Contract schedule or an inferred Freshness threshold

short_definition: The FabricOps orchestrator for validating and writing one governed target.
long_definition: pipeline_write() runs the applicable write-side checks, applies the governed load strategy, writes the target through FabricOps I/O, and records the resulting metadata only after the write succeeds.
preferred_usage: Use pipeline_write when referring to the public governed write orchestrator.
avoid_usage: a raw write helper

short_definition: The FabricOps orchestrator for reading a source and running the configured read-side governance checks.
long_definition: pipeline_read() resolves the source, reads it through the appropriate FabricOps I/O path, and runs the applicable read-side checks before returning data and inspection outputs to the notebook.
preferred_usage: Use pipeline_read when referring to the public governed read orchestrator.
avoid_usage: a raw read helper

short_definition: The column or column combination that uniquely identifies a row at the table's intended level of detail.
long_definition: FabricOps can suggest grain candidates from profile evidence and validate single or composite keys. The selected grain is stored with the Data Contract and used as governed table metadata.
preferred_usage: Use grain for the governed row-level key or key combination.
avoid_usage: primary key unless a physical database constraint is specifically meant

short_definition: A Guardrail that checks whether source data is current enough for the governed expectation.
long_definition: FabricOps Freshness evaluates a configured date or datetime column against the expected source refresh timing. It is separate from the notebook's Fabric scheduled refresh.
preferred_usage: Use freshness for the governed source-data recency expectation.
avoid_usage: scheduled refresh when the data-arrival expectation is meant

short_definition: The canonical metadata record for a governed table and its columns.
long_definition: FabricOps Data Catalogue metadata identifies governed tables and columns and stores the technical and enriched attributes used by profiling, contracts, guardrails, and other governance workflows.
preferred_usage: Use data catalogue for FabricOps table and column metadata.
avoid_usage: catalog when referring to the FabricOps metadata entity

short_definition: A check for unexpected changes to source data already consumed by a target.
long_definition: FabricOps compares the current source observation with the last committed observation for the same source, target, and environment. A new observation is committed only after the target write succeeds.
preferred_usage: Distinguish Source Drift from Freshness: Freshness asks whether data is current; Source Drift asks whether source history changed unexpectedly since this target last successfully consumed it.
avoid_usage: a freshness rule, change-required expectation, or load strategy

short_definition: The rule that one governed target table_id has one owning notebook writer.
long_definition: FabricOps records the logical writer notebook for a governed target. Production rejects a conflicting writer so independent pipelines do not write the same governed table with different assumptions.
preferred_usage: State that one governed target table_id should have one owning pipeline/notebook writer.
avoid_usage: a scheduling or distributed locking guarantee

short_definition: Microsoft's end-to-end analytics platform for data ingestion, transformation, real-time processing, analytics, and reporting.
long_definition: Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that brings together data ingestion, transformation, real-time processing, analytics, and reporting through integrated Fabric workloads over a shared data and compute foundation.
preferred_usage: Use the full product name on first mention.
avoid_usage: Fabric alone when ambiguous

short_definition: A collaborative container that brings related Fabric items together and controls access to them.
long_definition: A Microsoft Fabric Workspace is a collection of items in a shared environment designed for collaboration. It acts as a container for items such as lakehouses, warehouses, notebooks, semantic models, and reports, and provides controls for who can access them.
preferred_usage: Use workspace for the Fabric collaborative container that holds related items.
avoid_usage: tenant

short_definition: A Fabric data item that combines data-lake storage with warehouse-style querying for structured and unstructured data.
long_definition: A Lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric stores structured and unstructured data in one location using Delta Lake and supports analysis through both Apache Spark and SQL without requiring the data to be moved between separate systems.
preferred_usage: Use Lakehouse for the Microsoft Fabric item type.
avoid_usage: lake house

short_definition: A Fabric relational warehouse item for structured data with full transactional T-SQL capabilities.
long_definition: A Warehouse in Microsoft Fabric is an enterprise-scale relational warehouse on a data-lake foundation. It is designed for structured analytics and SQL-first data warehousing workloads and supports full transactional T-SQL capabilities.
preferred_usage: Use Warehouse for the Microsoft Fabric item type.
avoid_usage: SQL database when Fabric Warehouse is meant

short_definition: A Fabric code item and web-based interactive surface for developing and running data, Spark, and machine-learning workloads.
long_definition: A Microsoft Fabric Notebook is a primary code item and web-based interactive surface used to write and execute code, combine code with Markdown and visualizations, and develop data engineering, Apache Spark, and machine-learning workloads.
preferred_usage: Use notebook for the Microsoft Fabric notebook item.
avoid_usage: Jupyter notebook when the Fabric runtime matters

short_definition: A layered data architecture that progressively improves data from Bronze raw data through Silver validated and enriched data to Gold curated data.
long_definition: In Microsoft Fabric, Medallion Architecture organizes data into Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers so data becomes progressively more reliable and useful as it moves from raw ingestion through validation and enrichment to curated consumption. Fabric implementations can use Lakehouses, Warehouses, or a combination of Fabric data stores for these layers.
preferred_usage: Use medallion architecture for the Microsoft Fabric Bronze, Silver, and Gold layered architecture pattern.
avoid_usage: treating Bronze, Silver, and Gold as mandatory FabricOps store names

short_definition: Information that describes data and its technical, business, governance, or operational context.
long_definition: FabricOps metadata includes table and column structure, profiles, lineage, stewardship, agreements, contracts, enrichment, guardrails, and pipeline observations.
preferred_usage: Use metadata for information that describes or governs data.
avoid_usage: evidence or context when the specific metadata can be named

short_definition: A person or role responsible for maintaining the meaning, quality expectations, governance rules, classification, and appropriate use of data.
long_definition: A Data Steward helps maintain trusted governance context for data, including its business meaning, ownership or accountability, sensitivity, quality expectations, intended use, and governance decisions. FabricOps uses active Data Stewards as the provider and recipient parties in Data Agreements.
preferred_usage: Use data steward for the governance role responsible for maintaining trusted data context.
avoid_usage: owner when stewardship is meant

short_definition: How carefully data should be handled based on its confidentiality, privacy, business risk, or regulatory impact.
long_definition: Data Sensitivity describes the level of care and protection data requires based on confidentiality, privacy, business risk, or regulatory requirements. It can influence access, masking, sharing, retention, and other governance controls.
preferred_usage: Use data sensitivity for the handling classification of governed data.
avoid_usage: PII when the broader sensitivity concept is meant

short_definition: Information that can identify an individual directly or indirectly, on its own or when combined with other information.
long_definition: PII, or personally identifiable information, is information that can identify or be linked to an individual. Depending on the context and applicable policy, it may require controls such as restricted access, masking, minimization, or stricter handling.
preferred_usage: Use PII after personally identifiable information is clear from context.
avoid_usage: sensitive data when specifically referring to personal identifiers

short_definition: The governed definition of who is allowed to access data and under what conditions.
long_definition: Data Access describes who is permitted to use governed data, what level of access is appropriate, and what conditions or restrictions apply. Those requirements can be implemented through platform security controls such as permissions, RLS, OLS, or other mechanisms.
preferred_usage: Use data access for the governed access requirement, not a specific technical control.
avoid_usage: RLS or OLS when the broader access requirement is meant

short_definition: Whether data meets the expectations required for its intended use.
long_definition: In FabricOps, Data Quality Guardrails define deterministic checks such as completeness, allowed values, blocked values, ranges, uniqueness, and business-rule expressions.
preferred_usage: Use data quality in narrative text; use DQ after the meaning is established.
avoid_usage: quality alone when data quality is meant

short_definition: The rules and mechanisms that determine who can access data or system resources and what actions they can perform.
long_definition: Access Control is the broader set of rules and technical mechanisms used to determine who can access datasets, tables, columns, workspaces, files, or other resources and what actions they are allowed to perform.
preferred_usage: Use access control for the broad security concept; use a specific mechanism when that is what matters.
avoid_usage: data access when discussing the technical enforcement mechanism rather than the governed requirement

short_definition: A security method that controls which rows of data a user can see.
long_definition: Row-Level Security limits the rows available to a user based on identity, role, or access rules while allowing the same table or semantic model to serve different audiences.
preferred_usage: Use row-level security on first mention; use RLS after it is established.
avoid_usage: role-level security

short_definition: A security method that controls whether a user can access specific data objects such as tables or columns.
long_definition: Object-Level Security restricts access to specific data objects, such as tables or columns, so unauthorized users cannot access those objects even when they can access the wider semantic model or resource.
preferred_usage: Use object-level security on first mention; use OLS after it is established.
avoid_usage: row-level security when the restriction applies to tables or columns

short_definition: Named settings that control system or pipeline behaviour without changing the underlying implementation.
long_definition: FabricOps uses configuration to resolve environment-specific Fabric items and repeatable pipeline settings without embedding them throughout project logic.
preferred_usage: Use configuration in narrative text; use config in code-oriented shorthand.
avoid_usage: hard-coded values when behaviour should be configurable

short_definition: A repeatable sequence of steps that moves, transforms, validates, or writes data.
long_definition: In FabricOps, 02_pipeline provides the standard Read → Transform → Write flow, with governed orchestration around project-owned transformation logic.
preferred_usage: Use pipeline for an end-to-end data-processing flow.
avoid_usage: workflow when a data pipeline is specifically meant

short_definition: The Python API for Apache Spark.
long_definition: PySpark lets Python code use Apache Spark for distributed data processing. FabricOps uses PySpark in Fabric notebooks for repeatable data engineering and transformation workloads.
preferred_usage: Use PySpark when referring to Python code running on Spark.
avoid_usage: Python when Spark execution is the important distinction

short_definition: A measured summary of a dataset at a point in time.
long_definition: FabricOps profiling records characteristics such as row count, data types, nulls, distinct values, ranges, frequencies, and key candidates in metadata.
preferred_usage: Use profile for a summary of data characteristics at a point in time.
avoid_usage: profile evidence; catalogue evidence

short_definition: The defined structure of data, including its fields or columns and their data types.
long_definition: FabricOps uses schema expectations to compare the structure of governed data, including column names and data types, at the relevant read or write boundary.
preferred_usage: Use schema for the defined structure of data.
avoid_usage: layout when schema is meant

short_definition: A saved progress value used to identify data after the last successful incremental boundary.
long_definition: A watermark marks incremental progress. Its ordering, uniqueness, and tie-handling depend on the project-owned incremental design.
preferred_usage: Use watermark for the incremental boundary persisted on governed target rows.
avoid_usage: a second processing strategy outside the target load_strategy

short_definition: Processing multiple independent parts of a workload at the same time.
long_definition: Parallel Processing divides a workload so multiple tasks, partitions, or units of work can execute concurrently, which can reduce elapsed time when the workload and available compute support it.
preferred_usage: Use parallel processing for concurrent work across tasks, partitions, or workers.
avoid_usage: multithreading when the broader distributed-processing concept is meant

short_definition: Designing data structures and relationships so data can be stored, understood, and used effectively.
long_definition: Data Modelling is the practice of designing tables, fields, keys, relationships, and structures so data supports its intended analytical, operational, or reporting use.
preferred_usage: Use data modelling for the design of data structures and relationships.
avoid_usage: schema when the broader model design is meant

short_definition: A subdivision of data or workload used to organize storage or processing.
long_definition: A Partition groups part of a dataset or workload so it can be stored, scanned, processed, or managed independently. The term can refer to logical processing groups or physical storage organization depending on context.
preferred_usage: Use partition with enough context to distinguish logical processing from physical storage.
avoid_usage: assuming every partition is a FabricOps incremental partition

short_definition: Organizing stored data physically by one or more partition columns to improve management or data skipping.
long_definition: Physical Partitioning controls how data files are organized by partition values in storage. It is a target storage and performance concern, distinct from project-owned source filtering.
preferred_usage: Use physical partitioning when describing storage layout.
avoid_usage: incremental partition

short_definition: A load strategy that adds incoming rows to the target.
long_definition: FabricOps adds the prepared incoming rows without changing existing target rows.
preferred_usage: Use append for an additive target write strategy.
avoid_usage: incremental load when the read scope rather than write strategy is meant

short_definition: A load strategy that replaces the target data in the write scope.
long_definition: FabricOps replaces existing target data with the prepared output for the configured write scope.
preferred_usage: Use overwrite for a replacement target write strategy.
avoid_usage: SCD Type 1 when record-level matching and updates are meant

short_definition: Patterns for updating records while either replacing or preserving historical values.
long_definition: SCD1 updates the matched record in place. SCD2 preserves history by closing the previous version and writing a new version.
preferred_usage: Use slowly changing dimensions when discussing SCD patterns; introduce SCD before using the abbreviation alone.
avoid_usage: incremental load when the history-management pattern is meant

short_definition: The lifecycle state of a Data Contract version: Draft, Frozen, or Activated.
long_definition: A Draft can be edited, a Frozen version is immutable and ready for validation, and an Activated frozen version is approved for Production use and linked to a Data Agreement version.
preferred_usage: Use Draft, Frozen, and Activated for Data Contract lifecycle states.
avoid_usage: approved when the specific FabricOps contract state is meant

short_definition: A write-side check that confirms required governed expectations are present before publishing a target.
long_definition: FabricOps checks Guardrail Coverage before the target write so required contract protections are not silently omitted from the governed pipeline.
preferred_usage: Use guardrail coverage for the write-side completeness check over required governed protections.
avoid_usage: data quality coverage when the broader contract protection check is meant

short_definition: A human-readable requirement that describes how governed data should behave.
long_definition: FabricOps can translate a Business Rule into the smallest deterministic Data Quality rules it can resolve, falling back to a custom PySpark boolean expression when needed.
preferred_usage: Use business rule for the human-authored requirement before translation to executable Data Quality rules.
avoid_usage: DQ rule when referring to the original human-readable requirement

short_definition: A descriptive label that records the sensitivity or governance meaning of a table or column.
long_definition: FabricOps stores Information Classification as Enrichment. It provides governance context but does not apply masking, tokenization, bucketing, removal, or other runtime treatment by itself.
preferred_usage: Use information classification for descriptive sensitivity labels.
avoid_usage: Sensitive Data Guardrail when no runtime treatment is configured

short_definition: A recorded view of source state used as the baseline for Source Drift checks.
long_definition: FabricOps compares the current source state with the latest committed observation for the same source, target, and environment. A new observation is committed only after the target write succeeds.
preferred_usage: Use source observation for the persisted Source Drift baseline.
avoid_usage: profile when the drift baseline is specifically meant

short_definition: Metadata that records how governed data moves from source to target through a pipeline.
long_definition: FabricOps records source-to-target relationships from governed pipeline execution so a table's upstream and downstream paths can be traced.
preferred_usage: Use lineage for recorded source-to-target relationships.
avoid_usage: dependency when recorded data movement is meant

short_definition: The stable FabricOps identifier for one governed table.
long_definition: FabricOps uses table_id to resolve a governed table across metadata, Data Contracts, profiles, guardrails, lineage, and pipeline execution without relying on a physical Fabric item name alone.
preferred_usage: Use table_id when referring to the canonical FabricOps table identifier.
avoid_usage: table name when the governed identity is meant

short_definition: The resolved access people have to Fabric data after combining supported access paths.
long_definition: FabricOps combines Workspace roles, SQL endpoint grants, and OneLake security roles, then resolves principals to people where possible while retaining whether access came through an individual or group.
preferred_usage: Use effective data access for the combined resolved view of supported Fabric access paths.
avoid_usage: workspace access when multiple access paths are included
